original_question: Do there exist spherical orbifolds, meaning quotients of round spheres by finite isometry groups, that have exactly the same Laplace-Beltrami eigenvalues when multiplicities are ignored but have different Riemannian volumes?
target_in_paper: Question 1.1 in §1.1: the paper asks whether there exist examples of eigenvalue equivalent spherical orbifolds whose volumes differ; this is answered affirmatively by Theorem 1.2 in the introduction and again as Theorem 3.3 in §3.1, while Theorem 1.3 gives a stronger lens-space specialization. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31v.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target very closely: it is an existence question about spherical orbifolds, it compares Laplace-Beltrami eigenvalues with multiplicities ignored rather than full isospectrality, and it asks whether unequal volumes can occur. Your parenthetical gloss also matches the paper's quotient model for spherical orbifolds. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31v.pdf))
missing_details: The paper uses the technical term "eigenvalue equivalent" for orbifolds having the same set of Laplace-Beltrami eigenvalues, in contrast with "isospectral," which counts multiplicities. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31v.pdf))

A spherical orbifold is specifically a good Riemannian orbifold of the form S^d/Γ with Γ a finite subgroup of O(d+1); free action is not required. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31v.pdf))

To be fully stand-alone, one should say that the eigenvalues are those of the orbifold Laplacian induced from the round metric, equivalently obtained from Γ-invariant eigenfunctions on the sphere. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31v.pdf))

The paper's official question is purely existential: it asks for some examples, not necessarily a classification, not necessarily manifolds, and not specifically lens spaces. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31v.pdf))

The official formulation does not impose a same-dimension hypothesis on the two orbifolds, so adding one would make the question narrower than Question 1.1. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31v.pdf))
If one wants the volume notion explicit, the paper is using the quotient round metric; for S^d/Γ it records vol(S^d/Γ) = vol(S^d)/|Γ|. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31v.pdf))
refined_question: Do there exist spherical orbifolds S^{d_1}/Γ_1 and S^{d_2}/Γ_2, where each Γ_i is a finite subgroup of O(d_i+1) acting isometrically on the round sphere, such that the two orbifolds are eigenvalue equivalent—that is, their Laplace-Beltrami operators on L^2 have the same set of eigenvalues when multiplicities are ignored—but their Riemannian volumes are different? ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31v.pdf))
justification: The draft is essentially a paraphrase of Question 1.1 in §1.1. The nearby introductory context defines eigenvalue equivalence as equality of Laplace-Beltrami eigenvalue sets with multiplicities disregarded, and then asks exactly whether such spherical orbifolds can have different volumes. Section 2 supplies the paper's precise meaning of a spherical orbifold as a quotient S^d/Γ by a finite subgroup of O(d+1), and §3.1 proves the existential statement as Theorem 3.3. Theorem 1.3 is relevant nearby context because it gives a stronger positive result in the subclass of lens spaces, but it is not the narrowest official target of your draft. ([nyjm.albany.edu](https://nyjm.albany.edu/j/2024/30-31v.pdf))
